newsitem.title: UK: SW Water has up to 200 mln stg for purchases.
newsitem.headline: SW Water has up to 200 mln stg for purchases.

text.p: British water and sewerage firm South West Water has between 100 to 200 million stg to spend on non-core acquisitions, finance director Ken Hill told a press conference.
"There is 100-200 million pounds to spend on non-regulated earnings...they would have to be acquisitions of the right sort," he said.
South West Water's non-regulated businesses include waste management, construction projects and environmental testing.
Non-regulated businesses contributed 6.6 million stg to South West's interim pretax profits of 72.9 million stg and turnover made up 68.1 million stg of a total 196.5 million stg.

Chairman Keith Court said the company aimed to balance the turnover contributions of non-regulated and regulated businesses "as soon as we can," but added that returns on the non-regulated sector were not the same as for the core water services.

South West executives stressed that non-regulated businesses should improve profitability and therefore help the dividend payout, which it aims to show real increases of eight percent in coming years after a 20 percent rise expected this year.
It paid out a half year dividend of 11.8 pence, up 20 percent, as it had promised when two bids against it from Severn Trent and Wessex were blocked by the UK government in October.
"Clearly we will seek to beat the eight percent" if efficiencies achieved are better than expected, Hill said.
The company said dividend cover should be around 2.3 times by the end of the year and added that the balance sheet could cover both acquisitions and any potential share buy back.
It already has a mandate to buy back 10 percent of its shares but said it would only exercise that if it was in the interests of shareholders.
Gearing is around 36 percent, executives added.
The company has also promised a 15 stg rebate per customer by June 1997 but further rebates will depend on efficiency savings.
